answer: Allow each AI key one daily bid for lotus cargo at the wharf only if SHA-256(key, day, dawn beacon, nonce) has 24 leading zero bits. Validators recompute it; invalid proofs or repeat key/day bids are rejected. Every extra key needs a separate success: 2^24 hash trials on average per key each day. Key binding prevents proof reuse. Parallelism reduces delay, not expected work. Hashing is a recurring expense; hardware is reusable. This assumes secure hashing and a fresh beacon; ASICs and cheap power still let one owner buy many bids.
